definition: Count of payments this payer has already made to this payee, before T.
source: Payer's own ledger (payee_payers edge in production)
potential_leakage: None: counts completed past payments only; the payment under decision is excluded.
why_it_represents_fraud_behaviour: A first payment to a stranger is the setting for almost every scam; an established relationship is the strongest exculpatory signal a payer-side system has.
train_serve_parity: dataset_v2._relationship_row / features_v2.relationship_features - one function each side

definition: Days since this payer first paid this payee. NaN when there is no prior payment.
potential_leakage: None. NaN carries 'no relationship' rather than 0, which would read as 'started today'.
why_it_represents_fraud_behaviour: A relationship that has existed for months is hard to fake; a one-day-old one is what a mule account has.

definition: 1.0 always: the payer's own ledger is always readable.
why_it_represents_fraud_behaviour: Distinguishes 'no prior payments' (a measurement) from 'we could not look'.

definition: Days between the first and most recent NEW payer arriving at this payee.
available_at_pre_payment_time: Yes - maintained incrementally as payments are confirmed
potential_leakage: None: only edges observed before T. NaN when the payee was never observed.
why_it_represents_fraud_behaviour: A collection account gathers its payers in a burst; a shop gathers them over months.
train_serve_parity: graph_cache.graph_view -> features_v2.graph_features; generator mirrors the same fields

definition: Days between the payee's first and last observed activity.
why_it_represents_fraud_behaviour: Mule accounts are short-lived by design.

definition: Observed payments divided by observed lifespan.
why_it_represents_fraud_behaviour: Rate, not raw volume: a legitimate busy merchant has a high rate AND a long lifespan, which is why the two are separate features.

definition: Size of the connected component this payee sits in (persisted union-find).
potential_leakage: None: components only grow as edges are observed; no future edge is read.
why_it_represents_fraud_behaviour: Rings sit in small, tight components; popular merchants sit in large ones. Size alone is NOT a fraud signal, which is why it is a feature and not a rule.

definition: Largest number of payers this payee shares with any single other payee.
why_it_represents_fraud_behaviour: Ring members share their payer pool; unrelated merchants mostly do not.

definition: shared_payer_peak divided by the smaller of the two payer counts. NaN unless BOTH payees have >= 10 payers.
source: Bounded two-hop query, gated by MIN_PAYERS_FOR_OVERLAP
potential_leakage: None. The gate is the fix for the household false positive: five people paying two new shops produce ratio 1.0 over a tiny pool.
why_it_represents_fraud_behaviour: Normalised overlap, not raw degree - the form that survived the false-positive audit.
train_serve_parity: gate mirrored in generator and in features_v2.graph_features

definition: 1.0 when a graph row exists for this payee, else 0.0.
why_it_represents_fraud_behaviour: Keeps 'no graph position' distinct from 'a quiet graph position'.

definition: Binary: did this coercion pattern fire in the message (authority, urgency, fear, pay_request, credential_request, secrecy, remote_control, verify_payment, lure, contact_offline).
available_at_pre_payment_time: Yes: the payer pastes the message before paying
potential_leakage: None: the text is an input to the decision, not a product of it.
why_it_represents_fraud_behaviour: Scam messages apply pressure; the hard negatives in the corpus contain the same vocabulary, so a flag alone is weak evidence.
train_serve_parity: identical function called from generator and from features_v2

definition: Fitted logistic probability over the 10 patterns.
potential_leakage: None. Fitted on data/coercion_corpus.jsonl, which is independent of the transaction simulator.
why_it_represents_fraud_behaviour: Summarises pressure in one number; carries most of the message signal in the importance table.

definition: The production 0-100 score and the flag for 'only weak cues fired'.
why_it_represents_fraud_behaviour: weak_only is the hard-negative discriminator: bank notices trip weak cues and nothing else.
Scam text is often long, numeric (amounts, reference numbers) and shouty; so are some legitimate bank alerts, which is the point.

potential_leakage: None. Deliberately near-uninformative: 55% of legitimate rows and 62% of social-engineering rows carry one (AUC 0.40-0.60, asserted by test).
why_it_represents_fraud_behaviour: Distinguishes 'no text to read' from 'text with no pressure'.

definition: Whether the message carried a URL, the production analyser's score for the worst one, and whether the brand the URL claims differs from the payee.
potential_leakage: None. NaN when there is no message; 0.0 when there is a message with no link - a measurement.
why_it_represents_fraud_behaviour: Look-alike domains impersonating a bank are a scam staple; legitimate messages carry real biller and bank domains at a similar rate.

definition: Whether the payer stated a purpose, whether it is one of the scam-adjacent purposes, and whether a bill/investment is going to a personal phone address.
source: The payer's own selection from intent.INTENTS
potential_leakage: None: it is what the payer says before paying.
why_it_represents_fraud_behaviour: Victims often describe the scam truthfully ('a refund', 'I was asked to'); the mismatch case is a purpose that does not fit the recipient.

definition: 1.0 when the payee address is a personal phone number rather than a merchant handle.
why_it_represents_fraud_behaviour: Collection accounts are more often phone-number addresses; so are many honest small sellers, so it is weak on its own.
